note: Do Mi Sol goes from a bare drill (3 minutes, the cap) to a tune that skips to singing chord tones over chords, so the longer singing time is musical. The drill goes through D, A and C with the key chips on its heading, keys that keep a beginner's Do Mi Sol low on the staff, so the learner hears that the notes change and the pattern doesn't. The text walks the app (drone, mic, pitch line) and gives a reason for the syllables it asks for.

exercise.title: Do Mi Sol: skip, sing a tune, sing over chords
exercise.focus: Do Mi Sol in D, A and C · an easy skipping tune · Do and Sol over D and A
exercise.why: Most melodies move through the notes of a chord, so Do Mi Sol is the first set to know.

sections.text: Do Mi Sol over a drone

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff as a line. Sing {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} up and back down on the note names: they help you remember each sound. Then skip straight from {{1}} to {{5}}, holding each note until your line settles on it.
Then tap A at the top of this step, start again and sing the same {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} over the new drone, then the same in C. The notes change, the pattern doesn't.
Press Play to hear the tune, then start the mic and sing it on "la". Once it feels easy, sing it before you press Play.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the chords: D and A take turns, one bar each. On "ah", sing {{1}} (D) when the D chord comes round and {{5}} (A) when the A chord comes round. Then try {{3}} (F♯) over D instead.
